question: Should OpenClaw core adopt native cross-gateway session messaging for `sessions_send` and `sessions_spawn`, and if so should the supported shape be direct gateway peers, a remote-node registry, a relay, or a plugin/API extension first?
rationale: The request spans core Gateway trust boundaries, agent/session authorization, message delivery, session history, and new config surface, so code inspection can prove the gap but not choose the product/security contract.

options.title: Design core federation first
options.body: Keep the issue open and require a maintainer-approved FRD/security model before accepting a core `gateway.peers` or equivalent implementation.

options.title: Route through plugin/API extension
options.body: Keep core lean by defining any missing plugin, MCP, or node-registration surface needed for an external bridge, then close or redirect core implementation PRs once that path is viable.

options.title: Adopt the linked PR after repair
options.body: Use the existing implementation attempt as source work, but only after it is rebased, security-reviewed, and proven with a real multi-gateway run.

recommendation.title: Design core federation first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and require a maintainer-approved FRD/security model before accepting a core `gateway.peers` or equivalent implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the clearest repeated history on session-tool resolution, access, and delivery semantics in the implicated files.
